title: Enterprise FAPI 2.0 Authorization Server with JWE, DPoP (RFC 9449), PAR, and Dynamic Client Registration
objective: Implement an enterprise-scale Financial-grade API (FAPI 2.0) and OpenID Connect Authorization Framework in Python/FastAPI using SQLite and Cryptography. The framework is architected as a modular production service across core cryptographic engines, DPoP proof-of-possession verifiers, JWE token encryption, PAR orchestrators, dynamic client registries, and token family lineage managers. The system must support RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration, RFC 9126 Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR), RFC 7636 S256 PKCE, RFC 9449 DPoP token binding with ath hash verification and jti replay caching, JWE (JSON Web Encryption) encrypted refresh tokens, Strict Refresh Token Rotation (RTR) with multi-generational cascading family invalidation, OIDC UserInfo (RFC 6750), multi-key RSA/ECDSA JWKS rotation, RFC 7662 Introspection, RFC 7009 Revocation, and RFC 8628 Device Authorization Flow with concurrent polling state machines.
motivation: Financial-grade API (FAPI 2.0) specifications in Open Banking, Zero-Trust Identity, and Healthcare mandate asymmetric cryptographic proof-of-possession (DPoP), pushed authorization (PAR), encrypted token payloads (JWE), and strict multi-generational token rotation to eliminate token replay and theft. Building this production system requires deep multi-package software architecture, cryptographic mathematics, asynchronous concurrency management, and distributed state coordination.
difficultyExplanation:
1. Multi-Module FAPI 2.0 Architecture: Coordinating decoupled services across asymmetric key engines (RSA-2048/ECDSA P-256, RFC 7516 JWE encryption, RFC 7638 JWK thumbprints), DPoP proof verifiers (jti replay cache, htm/htu binding, ath token hash binding), PAR orchestrator (60s ephemeral single-use consume locks), and token family lineage databases.
2. Cryptographic DPoP Proof-of-Possession & JWE Encryption: Parsing client-generated ephemeral DPoP JWT proofs, verifying public JWK headers, calculating unpadded Base64URL SHA-256 access token hashes (ath), enforcing timestamp freshness, and decrypting/encrypting refresh tokens with AES-GCM JWE.
3. Concurrency Invariants & Multi-Generational Cascade: Handling multi-threaded concurrent token refresh races in SQLite, preventing double-spending, and instantly cascading revocation across 5+ generations of descendant access and refresh tokens upon replay detection.
environmentSummary: Python 3.11-slim container with FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pytest, Cryptography, PyJWT, HTTPX, SQLite3, and pre-configured multi-module package scaffolding across /app/core, /app/services, /app/api, and /app/models.
oracleStrategy: Modular reference implementation under solution/ featuring decoupled crypto engines, DPoP proof validators, JWE encryption pipelines, PAR managers, Dynamic Client Registration registries, SQLite token lineage databases, and REST route controllers.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh executing 8 rigorous multi-threaded hidden pytest test suites testing:
1. RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration with metadata and auth method configuration.
2. RFC 9126 Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR) and single-use request_uri exchange under concurrency.
3. RFC 7636 S256 PKCE authorization code grant with unpadded Base64URL validation.
4. Strict Refresh Token Rotation (RTR) with 5-generation token family replay attack invalidation.
5. RFC 9449 DPoP Proof-of-Possession validation, ath thumbprint binding, and jti replay rejection.
6. OIDC UserInfo endpoint (RFC 6750) and multi-key JWKS key rotation.
7. RFC 7662 Token Introspection and RFC 7009 Token Revocation.
8. RFC 8628 Device Authorization Flow with user verification and polling state transitions.
binarySuccessCondition: Passes 100% of all hidden test suites across all 8 FAPI 2.0 specification domains with full reward score >= 0.95.
